author: Mark Thompson
title: Ed Davey: Lib Dem Leader Boycotts King's Banquet Over Gaza
text:
Liberal Democrat Leader Ed Davey to Boycott State Banquet in Protest of Trump’s Gaza Policy A principled stand against inaction: The leader of the Liberal Democrats,Ed Davey,will forgo an invitation to a state banquet hosted by King Charles III in honor of former President Donald Trump,citing Trump’s perceived failure to leverage influence to end the ongoing conflict in gaza. The decision, announced today, underscores growing international pressure for a resolution to the humanitarian crisis.
Davey, who received the invitation to the dinner during Trump’s upcoming state visit to the United Kingdom, described the move as deeply arduous, stating it went against his instincts. However, he expressed a fear that without a deliberate act of protest, the issue of the Gaza crisis would be overlooked during the high-profile visit scheduled for late September.
“Boycotting the state banquet is not something I ever wanted to do, but I believe it is indeed the only way I can send a message to both Donald Trump and Keir Starmer that they cannot close their eyes and wish this away,” davey stated.
This state visit marks an unprecedented occasion, as Trump is the frist US president to be extended a second invitation for a state visit to the UK. While acknowledging the appropriateness of engaging with Trump, Davey emphasized the necessity of directly addressing the situation in Gaza.
“The humanitarian crisis in Gaza must stop. The famine must end. The hostages must be returned home,” Davey wrote in a piece published by The Guardian .”There is one man, more than anyone else, who has the power to make it happen. Donald Trump could do those things today if he chose to. He has more power than anyone else finally to force a ceasefire and put Israel and Palestine on the path to a lasting peace, with a two-state solution. But so far, he’s decided not to. Rather, he’s given Netanyahu his full support.”
Davey underscored the meaning of the invitation itself, acknowledging it as “one of the great privileges of being the leader of my party.” He explained that accepting an invitation from the King is a profound honor and a duty he takes seriously.”To refuse an invitation like this goes against all of my instincts. But having thought and prayed long and hard about it with Emily [Gasson, Davey’s wife], I have come to the conclusion that on this occasion I must refuse.”
Despite holding strong disagreements with Trump on a range of issues – including the war in Ukraine , his relationship with Vladimir putin , and his implementation of tariffs – Davey clarified that his boycott is solely focused on the situation in Gaza.
He acknowledged that Keir Starmer is correct to engage with the former president, but expressed a desire for a more assertive approach. “I fear we could have a situation where Trump comes to our country, is honoured with a lavish dinner at one of our finest palaces, and no one reminds him that he has the power to stop the horrifying starvation, death and captivities in Gaza.And no one uses this moment to demand that the US president picks up that phone to Netanyahu and the Qataris and does the right thing.”
Davey asserted his determination to utilize every available avenue as an opposition leader to address the acute suffering in Gaza. “I feel a duty to do whatever I can to make sure the people in Gaza are not forgotten during the pomp and ceremony. To make sure the UK makes Donald Trump’s personal responsibility for securing peace in Israel and Palestine an issue.”

Did you know? – This marks Trump’s second state visit invitation to the UK,an unprecedented occurrence for a US president. Pro tip: – The Gaza Strip is a self-governing Palestinian territory, approximately 25 miles long and 6 miles wide, bordering Egypt and Israel. Reader question: – Why is Trump seen as having influence? He maintains a close relationship with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
